newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up on latest report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up on latest report.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose around 1/4 point in early morning trade Tuesday as a tame inflation report drove Treasury bonds up sharply, but traders questioned how long the gains will be last.
"It remains to be seen how it's going to pan out, to be honest here, to see if there's going to be a lot of customer selling into it," a trader said.
And another player noted that not all dealers were positioned to profit by the big move up, as the market's recent bearish tone had led them to empty their shelves.
"Unfortunately, at the moment, we had completely decimated our inventory, cutting prices on things to get rid of them," the trader said.
But with the calender for new issues, especially competitive sales, fairly heavy, those sellers looked set to profit handsomely by the drop in fixed-income yields--at least initially.
"Futures are up almost a point, so they will probably over price everything and get hung up with balances," a trader said.
New issues slated to be sold on Tuesday totaled $439 million in 45 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings added up to $182 million in seven sales, with a $98 million Port of Corpus Christi, Texas, deal through Lehman Brothers topping the list.
On the competitive side, 38 sales totaling $257 million are on the schedule. A $70 million Clark County, Nev., deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
An additional 20 sales totaling $485 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they might price the bonds Tuesday, depending on market conditions.
Though the market had been bracing for the March Consumer Price Index to rise 0.2 percent, the latest report was not as strong, gaining only 0.1 percent.

The ex-food and energy segment, which aims to soften some of the data's volatility, had been predicted at up 0.3 percent in a consensus Reuters survey of economists. But it also was milder than expected, only firming 0.2 percent.
June Treasury bond futures climbed 27 ticks to 107-17/32, while the June municipal bond futures rose 30 ticks to 112-22/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 155 ticks.
In the secondary market, Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 percent, down one basis point.
And Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of February 2027, which have a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 96-5/8, up one-eighth of a point.
